g.title: Internet Attacker 2 roles; access details in Identified Actors Inject Input into Server Interpreters Attacker sends POST /rest/user/login with body {"email":"' OR '1'='1'--","password":"x"}, exploiting the absence of parameterized binding at routes/login.ts:34. C-01 · Authentication & Session Surface No account required Database access relies on concatenated queries (W-002) Unauthenticated remote attacker can log in as any user, including admin, by injecting SQL into the email field. Full authentication bypass, read access to all user sessions, and potential data modification via stacked queries (SQLite-dependent) are in scope. Declared sensitive assets — JWT signing key, TOTP secrets, MD5-hashed passwords — are all accessible after session establishment. Disclosure of customer information Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data

Internet Attacker 2 roles; access details in Identified Actors Bypass or Forge Authentication Attacker reads the full RSA private key literal from lib/insecurity.ts:23 in the publicly available repository. C-01 · Authentication & Session Surface No account required; Public source available Secrets are committed to source instead of a managed store (W-010) Permanent, offline authentication bypass for every user and role in the application. Any actor who clones the repository can forge tokens granting admin privileges, access all user accounts, manipulate orders, and read all sensitive data — the key cannot be invalidated without a code change and deployment. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data Customer account misuse and disclosure of private account data

Internet Attacker 2 roles; access details in Identified Actors Missing authorization grants admin and cross-user access A signed-in attacker puts another user's ID into the owner field of the request (req.body.UserId and the like); the query trusts it instead of the session identity, so the attacker reads or changes every other user's records — horizontal privilege escalation across all accounts. C-02 · Express.js REST API Backend No account required Authorization is implemented route by route (W-003) Technical consequence not established. Unauthorized administration and changes to protected business data Disclosure of customer information

Internet Attacker 2 roles; access details in Identified Actors Access Exposed Data and Secrets An unauthenticated attacker uploads a crafted ZIP archive whose entries contain path traversal sequences. The handler checks absolutePath.includes(path.resolve('.')) which only verifies the path starts within the application root, not within the uploads/complaints subdirectory. An entry with path ../../ftp/legal.md passes this check because the resolved application root is a prefix of the traversed path, allowing overwrite of files throughout the application directory tree. C-02 · Express.js REST API Backend No account required Input handling lacks enforced boundary validation (W-005) Attacker overwrites files anywhere within the application root including ftp/legal.md, server configuration, and other static content, enabling content tampering and potential command execution if a loadable file is overwritten. Disclosure of customer information

Internet Attacker 2 roles; access details in Identified Actors User-controlled input executes as server-side code Authenticate as any user and send a profile update request setting the username field to #{process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id').toString()}. C-02 · Express.js REST API Backend Regular account required Application data crosses into executable code (W-001) Remote code execution as the Node.js process; attacker can exfiltrate all environment variables, database contents, and private keys, or pivot to internal network services. Service disruption or compromise of application data

Internet Attacker 2 roles; access details in Identified Actors Inject Scripts into Victim Browsers An attacker submits a feedback entry with an HTML/script payload; when any user — including unauthenticated visitors — loads the About page, the gallery loop at lines 116-119 embeds feedback.comment verbatim in a template string and marks the result as safe with bypassSecurityTrustHtml, executing the payload for every visitor. C-03 · Angular Web Application (SPA) No account required; Victim interaction required Frontend rendering lacks enforced output encoding (W-009) Attacker's script executes in every About page visitor's browser, including unauthenticated users; for logged-in users, their JWT and session can be stolen. Customer account misuse and disclosure of private account data

Internet Attacker 2 roles; access details in Identified Actors Abuse Cross-Site Requests An attacker obtains a Google access_token for their own account, constructs a URL containing the access_token fragment targeting the app's OAuth route, and tricks a victim into following it; the SPA processes the token and logs the victim in as the attacker's Google identity because no state nonce is validated. C-03 · Angular Web Application (SPA) No account required; Victim interaction required OAuth sign-in requests are not bound to the user's browser session (W-007) Victim's session is authenticated as the attacker's Google identity; the attacker can read the victim's account data and perform purchases for the duration of that linked session. Customer account misuse and disclosure of private account data

Supply-Chain / Build Attacker 1 role; access details in Identified Actors Compromise the Build or Its Inputs Attacker publishes a malicious version of a transitive dependency within a semver range declared in package.json via maintainer account takeover. C-08 · CI/CD Pipeline Build or dependency access required Build pipeline trusts mutable third-party references (W-008) A compromised transitive dependency executes arbitrary code in CI and on every developer workstation, enabling secret exfiltration, backdoored release artifacts, or persistent compromise. Service disruption or compromise of application data
g.text: Compromise the Build or Its Inputs
